Geometry

Inside versus surface

The colored cloud is the boundary of the sRGB cube transformed into Oklab. An unmodified path may remain inside, leave it, or touch it. Mapping should constrain only what needs intervention—not force every point onto the surface.

Topology

The neutral axis

At zero chroma every hue collapses to the same point. Cartesian Oklab shows that collapse directly; a polar path can detour around the axis even when its endpoints are close in RGB.

Tradeoff

Smoothness costs identity

Hard projection preserves interior colors but creates a boundary kink. Soft compression bends earlier and changes more samples. Local MINDE tolerates only a perceptually small clipped difference.

Antipodes

Collapse before direction swaps

The antipodal gate progressively removes the polar bow as endpoint separation approaches 180°. At the ambiguous point it coincides with the Oklab chord, then reopens continuously on the other side.

Clockwise alternative

Rotate instead of collapse

The coral path keeps the polar bow and rotates its displacement clockwise around the oriented A→B Oklab chord. It avoids a side jump, but spends the third dimension and can create the deliberate lightness bulge shown here.
